text: VIFC-HCMC expands international partnerships to attract foreign capital from Singapore

HÀ NỘI - The Vietnam International Financial Centre in HCM City (VIFC-HCMC) is stepping up efforts to connect with international financial institutions, banks and investment funds to attract high-quality capital for infrastructure.

The VIFC-HCMC held a seminar on the sidelines of the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 in Singapore from November 18-20 to introduce the centre's development strategy, financial products and services ecosystem, and investment cooperation opportunities to the international financial community.

Associate Professor Nguyễn Hữu Huân, deputy chairman of the VIFC-HCMC Executive Authority, said the centre was prioritising four key product areas, including investment funds and asset management, international bond markets, financial technology (fintech), and commodity derivatives markets.

The centre also aims to expand specialised financial services in maritime, aviation and green finance, sectors with significant potential to support investment in infrastructure, logistics, energy and the country's green transition.
Huân said Việt Nam's ambition to achieve double-digit economic growth would require substantial capital mobilisation for transport infrastructure, energy and other key economic sectors.
VIFC-HCMC aims to develop diversified channels for raising capital and connect international investors with the financing needs of the Vietnamese economy.

The centre also seeks to combine traditional financial services with modern financial models while strengthening governance and risk management, gradually establishing a comprehensive international financial ecosystem to support economic development.
To attract foreign financial institutions and investors, VIFC-HCMC highlighted its flexible operating mechanisms, tax incentives and priority procedures for investment administrative processes.
In fintech, a regulatory sandbox is expected to provide a controlled environment for businesses to research, test and develop innovative financial products and services.
At the event, VIFC-HCMC and Silver Lion Enterprise Impact Singapore (SLEI) exchanged a letter of intent on the VIFC-SLEI Voyage initiative.

Under the proposed cooperation, the two sides plan to organise investment promotion activities and connect VIFC-HCMC with networks of banks, asset management organisations, venture capital funds and fintech companies in key international markets.

The initiative is expected to broaden the centre's international partnerships, diversify funding sources and attract foreign investors with strong financial capacity and a long-term cooperation outlook.
It will also create further opportunities for international financial institutions to provide products and services within the VIFC-HCMC ecosystem.

Nguyễn Thanh Tuyền, founder and CEO of SLEI, said emerging opportunities in deep technology, the green transition, maritime infrastructure and aviation are opening up prospects for long-term investment cooperation.

She said VIFC-HCMC can serve as a bridge between international financial resources and production, business and development investment activities in Việt Nam and direct capital towards sectors that generate tangible economic value.

Addressing the seminar, Vietnamese Ambassador to Singapore Trần Phước Anh said the continued development of the Vietnam-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership was creating opportunities to attract high-quality investment into infrastructure, green finance, clean energy and digital assets.
Through its engagement in Singapore, VIFC-HCMC will continue working to refine its operating framework, develop its membership ecosystem and expand its international partnership network. - VNS
